output.assessment: The current evidence establishes general Indian Standards for roof loads (IS 875 Part 2 specifies 1.5 kN/m² for accessible roofs and 0.75 kN/m² for inaccessible roofs) and the requirement for a structural stability certificate from a BMC-licensed structural engineer under DCPR 2034 and Section 353B of the MMC Act. evidence.claim: Under Indian Standard IS 875 Part 2, the minimum specified live (imposed) load for an accessible roof is 1.5 kN/m² (approx. 150 kg/m²), whereas for an inaccessible roof it is 0.75 kN/m² (75 kg/m²).
evidence.production_implication: The motorcycle, ramps, and crew will far exceed standard roof live loads (1.5 kN/m²). A rigorous structural engineering assessment and reinforcement are mandatory to safely distribute these concentrated dynamic loads.

evidence.claim: Structural safety and load-bearing capacity must be calculated by a qualified structural engineer to Indian Standards and verified via a formal structural stability (safety) certificate.
evidence.production_implication: The production must hire a BMC-licensed structural engineer to perform load calculations and issue a structural stability certificate specifically for the stunt setup.

evidence.claim: Under Section 353B of the MMC Act 1888, buildings in use for more than 30 years within the Greater Mumbai limit must undergo a compulsory structural audit by an MCGM-registered structural engineer.
evidence.production_implication: If older buildings are selected for the rooftop stunt, the production must verify that the building has a valid, up-to-date structural audit clearance under Section 353B.

evidence.claim: Under Mumbai's DCPR 2034, internal modifications or temporary structures are subject to obtaining a structural stability certificate from a Licensed Structural Engineer.
evidence.production_implication: Any temporary ramps, platforms, or rigging structures erected on the rooftops will require formal sign-off from a licensed structural engineer.

evidence.claim: The Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM/BMC) processes film shooting permissions, including temporary structures, through a common application form via the State Single Window System.
evidence.production_implication: All permissions for the rooftop shoot and temporary stunt structures must be routed through the Maharashtra State Single Window System for BMC clearance.
